event_confirmation: Company GlobeNewswire release 2026-10-26: Q3 call Monday 2026-11-09 08:30 ET (summarised at https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/HRTX/heron-therapeutics-q3-2026-results-call). EarningsWhispers lists it as confirmed for 2026-11-09 before the open.
conviction_note: The findings net to about +0.7: CINVANTI exposure to Azurity's approved 505(b)(2) copy (-2.0) and covenant pressure (-0.8) against the Long Grove deal terms arriving in the 10-Q (+1.5), APONVIE/ZYNRELEF growth against a bar already reset to the Q2 level (+1.0) and a crowded short that is already covering (+1.2). The scaled number is p_up 49 x abs 20 = -0.4, a near coin flip. The two disagree in sign only by tenths, because the largest single risk (CINVANTI erosion) is a proxy and it is offset by positioning. The scale is large (median prior reaction 19.9%) and the direction is not known.
bar: Q3 2026 net revenue about $37.5-37.6M and EPS -$0.03. Two estimate sources agree: Benzinga $37.5M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HRTX/earnings-forecasts) and EarningsWhispers $37.6M / -$0.03 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/HRTX). There is no company guide: FY2026 guidance ($173-183M revenue, $10-20M adj. EBITDA) was withdrawn on 2026-08-10 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/818033/000119312526341300/hrtx-ex99_1.htm). The bar is flat against Q2's actual $37.7M. Q2 missed a $42.2M bar and Q1 also missed, so consensus has been reset down to the last print.
positioning_check: Short interest is 36.74M shares, about 19% of the 189.85M shares outstanding, with 14.2 days to cover on 2.58M average volume, per massive.com quoting FINRA as of 2026-10-15 (https://massive.com/quote/hrtx). An earlier reading of 46.02M short and 17.3 days to cover at 2026-09-30 (same site, via search snippet) means shorts covered about 9M shares in the first half of October. Some of the position may be a convertible hedge (the $33.9M convertible notes are partly held by Rubric), but at $0.29 a hedge delta should be small. No usable option chain exists (the baseline reads empty_chain), so there is no skew. The tape is at $0.29: -29% over 20 days, -80.5% from the 52-week high, 7% above the 52-week low, and +3.6% over 5 days. Market cap is about $53M against about $125M+ of Hercules and convertible debt, so the equity behaves like an option. The short is crowded, so the negatives were shrunk.

findings.finding: CINVANTI was $21.8M, 58% of Q2 revenue, and down 9.7% YoY. Its two asserted patents ('255 and '520) were held invalid for Azurity on 2026-06-01. FDA approved Azurity's polysorbate-80-free, ready-to-use aprepitant injectable emulsion (505(b)(2), 130 mg/18 mL) on 2026-06-16. Heron's Federal Circuit appeal (No. 26-2004, filed 2026-07-06) is pending, and no stay of market entry was found. Q3 is therefore the first full quarter in which a direct CINVANTI copy was free to launch. A launch or wholesaler listing was NOT found, and on the Q2 call management said no generic had launched.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 2026 invalidity ruling took the stock down 45.6% the next session (https://www.quantisnow.com/insight/heron-therapeutics-downgraded-by-needham-6585930). Q2's revenue miss and guidance withdrawal, both tied to CINVANTI generic risk, gave -30.6% on 2026-08-10 (baseline). CINVANTI-driven misses have been sold hard.
findings.why_not_priced: The ruling and the approval are public and largely priced into a $0.29 stock. What is not visible is the size of Q3 CINVANTI erosion, if any, and whether Azurity shipped. A flat $37.5M consensus against Q2's $37.7M implies only modest CINVANTI decline offset by ZYNRELEF/APONVIE growth. If the market expected a material Azurity share grab in Q3, consensus would sit visibly below Q2. Net of the rest of the company: ZYNRELEF ($11.1M, +35%) and APONVIE ($4.3M, +74%) would have to add about $1-2M sequentially to offset a 5-10% CINVANTI decline.
findings.independence: Azurity's FDA approval release, 2026-06-25 (https://investor.wedbush.com/wedbush/article/gnwcq-2026-6-25-azurity-pharmaceuticals-announces-fda-approval-of-aprepitant-injectable-emulsion-expanding-access-to-critical-supportive-oncology-care), and the ONN report of 2026-06-30 (https://www.oncnursingnews.com/view/fda-approves-ready-to-use-aprepitant-injectable-emulsion-for-cinv). Neither confirms a launch, so this is an inference about the quarter, not a measured number.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-23 Heron signed a multi-product Development and License Agreement with Long Grove Pharmaceuticals, plus Capstone as backstop. Heron gets exclusive US rights to sell certain products and pays regulatory/sales milestones and royalties. Long Grove is the company that sent Heron a Paragraph IV notice on CINVANTI on 2026-06-26, and Heron sued it in Delaware on 2026-08-07. The full agreement, and probably the fate of that CINVANTI challenge, is to be filed with the Q3 10-Q, which normally lands with the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print on this line. The stock rose from $0.29 (Sep 28) to $0.31 on the 8-K day (2026-09-29, 3.4M shares) and $0.36 by Oct 1, then gave it all back to $0.29 by late October (Yahoo daily bars, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HRTX?range=6mo&interval=1d).
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K gave no products, no dollar amounts and nothing about the CINVANTI suit. The stock round-tripped the initial pop, so the market is not crediting it. If the deal were priced as a settlement that removes a second CINVANTI challenger and adds products to an idle sales force, the October gain would have held. Terms arrive with the 10-Q/release.
findings.independence: Heron's Q2 10-Q documents the Long Grove Paragraph IV notice and the 2026-08-07 suit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/818033/000119312526341301/hrtx-20260630.htm). That is the same company's filings, so it is not independent of the issuer. Whether the license settles the suit is an inference.

findings.finding: The Hercules facility was amended on 2026-08-07 (Waiver, Consent and Fourth Amendment). It waived the June 30 minimum-net-revenue and minimum-adjusted-EBITDA tests, required a voluntary paydown ($13.5M at signing, up to $4M more by 2026-09-15), and added monthly revenue, EBITDA and cash covenants through 2027. That leaves roughly $24-29M of cash against about $91M+ of term debt, $33.9M of convertibles and $6.9M of equity at June 30. Revenue missed internal plans in both Q1 and Q2, so the Q3 10-Q's covenant-compliance and going-concern language is a live risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's print, which carried the covenant reset alongside the guidance withdrawal, fell 30.6% (baseline). The two cannot be separated.
findings.why_not_priced: The covenant levels are not in the public text, so nobody can compute headroom. The forward-looking statements already name 'ability to continue as a going concern without additional funding' as a risk. A formal substantial-doubt paragraph would be new. If the market had priced a waiver or a going-concern flag, the stock would trade at a pure option value, and arguably it already does at $53M market cap. A secondary summary says management expressed confidence in meeting the reset covenants even with a CINVANTI generic (unverified, https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/HRTX/q2-2026/). The money here buys debt reduction and covenant room, not a ramp (the sales-force expansion is paused), so the sign is negative, and the finding is sized small because it is covenant inference.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/818033/000119312526341300/hrtx-ex99_1.htm) states the $13.5M paydown and the covenant reset. That is the same issuer, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: The bar is now flat at Q2's actual level ($37.5-37.6M vs $37.7M). Q2 showed ZYNRELEF +35% YoY ($11.1M, average daily units +19%) and APONVIE +74% ($4.3M, 23% share of the surgical NK-1 segment), and APONVIE's permanent J-code J8502 has been active since 2026-04-01. Q3 is APONVIE's second full quarter on a permanent J-code, which supports continued growth of the acute-care franchise into a bar that asks for none.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Acute-care growth has not been paid for. Q2 had acute care +43.9% YoY and still fell 30.6% because total revenue missed. Q1 missed and fell 20.7%. The +11.1% on 2026-02-26 came with a pre-released Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is two agreeing estimates, both reset to the last quarter, so a merely flat quarter no longer misses. That is the first time in 2026 the bar has not been above the run-rate. If the market expected continued acute-care growth to beat, the 20-day run-up would not be -29%. The rest of the company (CINVANTI, 58%) is what decides it, and that is netted in the CINVANTI finding.
findings.independence: The APONVIE J-code activation was reported in Heron's Q1 2026 materials (https://ir.herontx.com/node/17736). Same issuer. No independent script or claims series was reachable.

findings.finding: Short interest was 36.74M shares, about 19% of shares outstanding, with 14.2 days to cover at 2026-10-15, down from about 46.0M and 17.3 days at 2026-09-30. A crowded short is covering into a print where the bar has been reset to flat, on a $0.29 stock 7% above its 52-week low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earlier squeezes are not documented. The +19.9% (2025-02) and +13.6% (2025-05) up-moves show this name can gap up double digits on a non-disappointing print.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is visible, but it acts as a mechanism, not a price. With 14 days to cover, any print that is not a miss forces buy-ins from a short base nearly 15x average daily volume. If shorts had finished covering, short interest would be back near the 2025 level, not at 19% of shares.
findings.independence: Curvedtrading shows 40.5M short and 11.1 days to cover at 2026-06-30 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/hrtx/). The settlement dates differ, but the short has been large all year.

findings.finding: Heron has been 'considering strategic alternatives' since 2026-08-10 with no timetable, and the Q3 print is the first scheduled update. Market cap is about $53M against about $125M+ of secured and convertible debt and $6.9M of equity. Any outcome disclosed (a sale, an asset sale, a process ended or a recapitalisation) is two-sided for the common: a sale could pay a premium, or mostly cover creditors.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement itself came with the -30.6% Q2 reaction. There is no outcome history.
findings.why_not_priced: No update has been given since August. The sign cannot be called, so it is sized at 0 and carried in abs_move_pct.

findings.finding: Insiders bought nothing at $0.28-0.36. The October and November Form 4s for the CEO (Collard, 2026-10-30/31) and the CFO (Duarte, 2026-10-19) are only RSU vesting with share withholding (code F at $0.28 and $0.36), with no open-market purchases while the strategic review runs.
findings.why_not_priced: It is weak evidence. Insiders may be restricted during a strategic review, so the absence of buying is barely informative.
findings.independence: The CFO's Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/818033/000119312526427545/ownership.xml) shows the same kind of transaction.

outside_window.finding: Nasdaq minimum-bid-price notice of 2026-06-25: the cure period runs to 2026-12-22, and the company may seek a second 180 days with a reverse split if necessary. A reverse-split proposal could be announced with the print, but the deadline itself is after the window.
The Federal Circuit appeal of the Azurity invalidity ruling (No. 26-2004, filed 2026-07-06, opening brief due 2026-09-04) will not be decided inside the window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree with. The run-up is -29% over 20 days. The negatives (CINVANTI exposure, covenants) agree with that drawdown and are probably mostly in a $0.29 price. The positives (bar reset to flat, Long Grove terms, a crowded short) cut against it. The net is close to zero on a name that moves about 20%.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, 19% of shares and 14 days to cover): shrank the two negatives, CINVANTI/Azurity -2.5 to -2.0 and covenant -1.0 to -0.8, and moved p_up from 48 to 49.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): the CINVANTI finding stays at -2.0 net of ZYNRELEF/APONVIE growth, with the offset written into why_not_priced. No further cut, to avoid stacking.
Rule 5 / core (proxy evidence): positioning trimmed from +1.5 to +1.2, because positioning is a mechanism and not a company number.
Rule 8 (thin coverage, size on the name's own distribution): abs_move_pct raised from 18 to 20, the median prior reaction 19.9%.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): asked what the Hercules paydown buys. The answer is covenant room and survival, with no ramp (sales force paused), so the sign stays negative and the size small.
Rule 6 (bar): two agreeing sources ($37.5M / $37.6M), so no cap was needed. The Nasdaq deadline and the Federal Circuit appeal stay in outside_window.
